name: כפולה משותפת מינימלית של שני מספרים (באנגלית)
questiontext: Find the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of \({{CT:0}}\) and \({{CT:1}}\).    [[input:ans]] [[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
<html>
To find the LCM of two numbers first factor into primes:

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:2}}, \]
\[ {{CT:1}} = {{CT:3}}. \]

Then we define the LCM as the product of the ALL the primes in both \({{CT:0}}\) and \({{CT:1}}\) (However if a prime appears in both \({{CT:0}}\) and both {{CT:4}} then we only count it once.) By doing this we obtain the LCM, \({{CT:5}}\).
</html>

on_true.feedback: You appear to have counted factors appearing in both {{CT:6}} and {{CT:4}} twice. By doing this you have simply found the product of {{CT:6}} and {{CT:4}}. The Lowest Common Multiple is only ever the product of two numbers if those two numbers are co-prime.
